categories.main_business_segments: Tsubaki Nakashima operates two main business segments: the Precision Component Business, which manufactures and sells precision balls and rollers (accounting for approximately 98.9% of revenue), and the Blower & Real Estate Business, which produces and sells medium and large centrifugal blowers (about 1.1% of revenue). The company has recently classified its linear motion (ball screw and ball way) business as a discontinued operation.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include advanced precision machining and automated production methods for high-quality steel, ceramic, carbide, glass, and plastic balls, as well as precision rollers. It emphasizes ultra-high-precision, cost-effective manufacturing, and maintains a broad inventory for rapid delivery. For blowers, it utilizes finite element analysis and real-world testing to develop high-efficiency, low-noise products.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers are major bearing manufacturers and large industrial companies, with end markets including automotive, industrial machinery, home appliances, wind power, semiconductors, and medical devices. The top three customers (ABSKF, Schaeffler, NTN) account for a significant portion of sales, reflecting a high degree of customer concentration.
categories.geographic_coverage: Tsubaki Nakashima operates globally with manufacturing and sales bases in Japan, the United States, Italy, Poland, Slovakia, the Netherlands, Bosnia & Herzegovina, the UK, China, Thailand, India, and Taiwan. Major revenue contributions come from China, the US, Italy, Poland, and Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company is positioned midstream in the supply chain, supplying precision components (balls and rollers) that are critical inputs for downstream manufacturers of bearings and various industrial and consumer products.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening cost competitiveness, optimizing the global manufacturing footprint, and focusing resources on high-growth and high-profit segments, especially ceramic balls for EVs and eco-friendly applications. R&D is directed at automation, ultra-precision processing, and sustainable manufacturing, with a strong emphasis on ESG, decarbonization, and diversity.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of manufactured products (precision balls, rollers, and blowers) to industrial customers, with sales recognized at the point of delivery. There is no significant recurring or service-based revenue model.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include global precision component and bearing part manufacturers, particularly from China and India, which are intensifying price competition. Tsubaki Nakashima positions itself as a global leader in high-precision, high-quality components, but faces ongoing margin pressure from emerging market players.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2024, consolidated revenue was 75.9 billion yen, with operating profit of 0.8 billion yen and net profit attributable to owners of 0.9 billion yen. The company has experienced recent revenue contraction and significant profit volatility, but targets a return to growth and higher profitability by 2029 (with goals of 87 billion yen in revenue and 10 billion yen in operating profit). Total assets are 174.7 billion yen, and the company employs 2,776 people.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tsubaki Nakashima emphasizes its ability to deliver over 20,000 types of high-quality, high-precision balls and rollers with short lead times, supported by global inventory and manufacturing. Its ceramic balls offer superior durability, insulation, and eco-friendly performance, making them essential for next-generation applications such as EVs, wind power, and semiconductors. The company differentiates through quality, breadth of product range, and rapid, reliable supply.
